title: Pre-Regional Mathematical Olympiad
text:
The Pre-Regional Mathematical Olympiad (Pre-RMO) is the first of series of math tests held in India to determine the participants of the IMO. It is usually held in August. High-scoring participants move on to take the India Regional Mathematical Olympiad.

Pre-RMO
Region: India

Difficulty: 2-5

Structure[edit]

From 2017 to 2019 the test had 30 questions and lasted for 3 hours. In 2021-22, the contest was reduced to 12 questions. Since 2021-22, PRMO and RMO have been merged into IOQM. Each answer is a one or two digit positive integer. The test covers pre-college math topics, especially algebra, number theory, combinatorics, and geometry. In particular, none of the problems require calculus or statistics.

In 2023, RMO has been brought up again and PRMO has been renamed to IOQM(Indian Olympiad Qualifier in Mathematics). In 2023, the test has 30 problems to be solved in 3 hours with 10 problems each of 2 marks, 3 marks and 5 marks contributing to the total of 100 maximum marks.

Recommended Resources[edit]

Comprehensive & Foundational[edit]

  • An Excursion in Mathematics (Editors: M. R. Modak, S. A. Katre, V. V. Acharya, V. M. Sholapurkar): Published by Bhaskaracharya Pratishthana, this is a staple for building a solid Olympiad base.
  • Challenge and Thrill of Pre-College Mathematics (V. Krishnamurthy, C. R. Pranesachar, K. N. Ranganathan, B. J. Venkatachala): A comprehensive text covering theory across all major topics.
  • Problem Primer for the Olympiads (C. R. Pranesachar, B. J. Venkatachala, C. S. Yogananda): Excellent for transitioning from school mathematics to competition-level problem solving.
  • IOQM Mathematics by Prashant Jain (PJ Sir): A modern guide specifically tailored to the current IOQM exam pattern.
  • Mathematical Circles (Russian Experience) (Dmitri Fomin, Sergey Genkin, Ilia Itenberg): A world-class resource for developing mathematical intuition and "thinking like an Olympian."

Algebra & Inequalities[edit]

  • Higher Algebra by Hall and Knight: A classic for mastering sequences, series, and theory of equations.
  • Functional Equations by B. J. Venkatachala: A specialized text for a topic frequently appearing in RMO and INMO levels.
  • Inequalities: An Approach Through Problems by B. J. Venkatachala: A rigorous treatment of algebraic inequalities.
  • Pathfinder for Olympiad Mathematics by Vikash Tiwari and V. Seshan: Known for its high-difficulty problem sets.
  • Advanced Problems in Mathematics (Black Book) by Vikas Gupta and Pankaj Joshi: Targeted practice for high-level algebra and functions.
  • Vedantu IOQM book by all Vedantu master teachers

Geometry[edit]

  • Euclidean Geometry in Mathematical Olympiads (EGMO) by Evan Chen: A modern favorite for students moving toward national and international levels.
  • Geometry Revisited by H. S. M. Coxeter and S. L. Greitzer: Covers elegant theorems beyond the standard school curriculum.

Number Theory & Combinatorics[edit]

  • Elementary Number Theory by David M. Burton: The most accessible entry point for congruences and divisibility.
  • Principles and Techniques in Combinatorics by Chen Chuan-Chong and Koh Khee-Meng: A systematic guide to counting and combinatorial principles.
  • Problem Solving Strategies by Arthur Engel: A legendary resource for mastering diverse topics, particularly combinatorics and invariance.
  • An Exploration of Olympiad Combinatorics by Rushil Mathur: A highly recommended modern text for self-study.
